ways.personalDesc: Meeting someone ends in one tap: your contact is saved to their phone there and then. No paper card, no reading a number out, no typos.
ways.businessDesc: It goes on a table, in a room or at the till: menu, call button, requests and statistics. Unlike a printed menu it is edited at any moment and counts how often it was opened.

how.title: Three steps
how.step2Title: Pick a thing to carry it
how.step1Body: Random, or the one you want. The number is yours for life — lose the card and the replacement carries the same number.
how.step2Body: Card, ring, band, windscreen tag, pet tag. One or several — all of them answer to the same number.
how.step3Body: They hold their phone to it and your profile opens. One press saves your contact. You get a record of it — who, when, where.

devices.note: One number, several things. All of them open the same profile.
devices.title: Devices
devices.lead: The number is yours. The device is where you carry it. Take one or take all of them — they open the same profile.
devices.chip: NTAG213, 144 bytes — enough for the link and nothing spare
devices.battery: No battery. Nothing to charge, nothing to replace
devices.app: No app to install — not for you, not for whoever taps it
devices.rewrite: Rewrite the number whenever you like. The object stays the same

card.name: Card
card.tagline: Earns its place in the wallet
card.body: Bank-card size, 0.8 mm thick. Matte black PVC — it does not hold fingerprints and does not scuff in a pocket. The name and number are laser-engraved rather than printed: ink wears off, an engraving does not. Nobody hands this one back out of politeness.

ring.name: Ring
ring.tagline: You shake a hand, the profile opens
ring.body: Ceramic over stainless steel. The tap happens inside the handshake, so there is no separate gesture — and that is the end of looking for a wallet. We send a sizing strip before the order: paper, five minutes. Guess wrong and we exchange it once, free.
ring.spec3: Stays on in water, stays out of the way in the gym

band.name: Band
band.tagline: Lives on the wrist, works on the wrist
band.body: Italian leather, steel magnetic clasp. Wears under a watch or instead of one. Sweat and rain are fine; the leather darkens over time, which is not a fault — that is how leather ages. You cut it to length yourself, and the ruler is in the box.
band.spec3: Holds up to sweat and rain

cartag.name: Car tag
cartag.tagline: Behind the windscreen, instead of your number
cartag.body: A black plate that sits under the glass. Instead of a phone number on display for everyone: whoever taps it writes or calls, and never sees the number. Parked somewhere awkward, that person reaches you directly — before anyone calls a tow truck.
cartag.spec2: Does not fade in sun or crack in frost

pettag.name: Pet tag
pettag.tagline: If they wander off, whoever finds them taps
pettag.body: A light tag for the collar. Whoever finds them taps a phone and sees your name, your number and a note about medication. No app — which is exactly why it works: the finder installs nothing. Change the details whenever you like; the tag stays the same tag.
pettag.spec1: 28 mm, 6 g — light enough for a small dog
pettag.spec2: Steel clip, will not work loose off the collar
pettag.spec3: Rain and swimming pools are fine

stand.name: Stand
stand.tagline: Sits on the table, the guest taps it themselves
stand.body: For a cafe, a salon, a reception desk. It sits on the table: menu, review, Telegram channel — where it leads is your call. NFC on one face and a QR on the other, because not every phone has NFC switched on. It has weight, so it stays put when a sleeve catches it.
stand.spec1: NFC on one face, QR on the other
stand.spec3: Change the link whenever you like

faq.title: Questions
faq.q1: What is a number and how is it priced?
faq.q2: How does the NFC device work?
faq.q3: What does it do for a cafe or a hotel?
faq.q4: How many staff can I add?
faq.a1: A number is a unique code of three letters and three digits — MYN042, say — and it becomes the address of your profile. The price starts from a base and rises with how rare the letters and digits are. Type any combination on the pricing page and its price appears straight away.
faq.a2: Hold the device — card, ring or bracelet — to somebody's phone and your Flex profile opens by itself. Nobody installs an app. Phones without NFC use the QR code instead.
faq.a3: Every table or room gets its own QR code and its own NFC tag. A guest taps it, the menu or service list opens, and from there they call a waiter, ask for the bill or leave a review. The request arrives on the phone by the till with a sound and with the table number on it. The monthly report shows the average time to answer and which table calls most.
faq.a4: The team plan is sold by the seat, minimum five. A seat belongs to the company rather than to a person: when somebody leaves it frees up and goes to the next hire.
faq.a5: Payme for a number and a personal subscription. Cafes, hotels and companies pay by invoice and bank transfer: the document is issued in the cabinet and the subscription is extended when the money arrives.

personal.metaDescription: Three letters and three digits — bought once and yours for life. Engraved on a card, a ring or a band; a tap opens your profile.
personal.titleA: You buy the number once and it stays yours —
personal.lead: This is not a subscription to a number. You buy it and you keep it: lose the card and the replacement carries the same number. Card, ring, band — whichever you take, they all open one profile.
personal.heroPhotoAlt: A Flex card held against a phone
personal.pickLead: Three letters of your name, your company, or simply the three you like. If it is free you see the price here; if it is taken you see who has it.
personal.formulaTitle: How the price is worked out
personal.formula: {base} × how rare the letters are × how rare the digits are
personal.rule1: Words people know cost more: VIP, CEO, OSH, UZB.
personal.rule2: So do three of the same letter or digit: AAA, 777.
personal.rule3: Runs and mirrors cost more than plain digits: 123, 121.
personal.blockedNote: Some combinations are not for sale at all — the abbreviations of state bodies, and words used as insults.
personal.priceLead: Three parts, because they are three different things: the number is scarce, the object is manufactured, and the profile runs every month.
personal.numberNote: Priced by how rare it is. You pay once — there is nothing to renew and no monthly charge on it.
personal.deviceNote: Card, ring, band, windscreen tag, pet tag. Take one or take five — all of them answer to the same number.
personal.planNote: Keeping your page up is free. The monthly part pays for statistics, the contacts you collect, and links without a limit.
personal.plansTitle: What the monthly part is for
personal.plansLead: The profile runs every day: a server, a domain, backups. So there is a free half and a paid half — and the number is yours on both.
personal.freeNote: Included in the price of the number
personal.free1: Your profile page and a QR code
personal.premiumNote: For the profile working in full
personal.premiumYear: {yearly} so'm a year — two months free
personal.prem2: Day-by-day statistics — which link, and where from
personal.prem3: The contacts you collect, exported to Excel
personal.prem4: Your own background picture and the gold trim
personal.prem5: The Flex line comes off the page
personal.lapse: Stop paying and the profile does not go dark — it falls back to the standard plan. The number is yours either way.
personal.arrivesLead: The object and the profile arrive together: open the box, tap it, it works.
personal.arrive1Title: The object, engraved with your number
personal.arrive1Body: Your name and number are cut in with a laser rather than printed on top: ink wears off, an engraving does not.
personal.arrive2Body: That is where the profile lives. A link sent in a message and a tap on the object open the same page.
personal.arrive3Title: A QR code on the back
personal.arrive3Body: For phones without NFC, or with it switched off. Whoever taps it installs nothing.
personal.arrive4Body: Links, services, photograph — you change them yourself. The object stays the object; what is behind it is what changes.
personal.delivery: We deliver across Tashkent. Payment through Payme.
personal.arrivesPhotoAlt: A card, a ring and a band on one table
personal.q1: What if my phone has no NFC?
personal.a1: The QR code on the back works — the camera opens it. On an iPhone NFC is on by itself; on Android it is switched on in the settings.
personal.q2: If I lose the card, do I lose the number?
personal.a2: No. The number belongs to your account, not to the object. Order a new one and it is engraved with the same number; switch the lost one off in the cabinet and it stops working.
personal.q3: What happens if I stop paying monthly?
personal.a3: The profile stays up, it just returns to the standard plan: five links, overall statistics. The number stays yours and is never sold to anybody else.
personal.q4: Will everybody see my phone number?
personal.a4: You decide what stands on the profile. You can hide the phone number and leave only a message or Telegram button — that is exactly how the windscreen tag is meant to work.
personal.q5: Can I move to a different number later?
personal.a5: You can buy another one, but it is another number: the first stays yours as well. So take your time — check it first, then order.
personal.orderLead: Pick the number, pick the object, pay. We do the rest.
personal.orderStep1Body: While the payment is pending, that number is sold to nobody else.
personal.orderStep2Body: Card, ring, band, or several at once. The name and number are engraved.
personal.orderStep3Body: Through Payme. Once it clears, the number is transferred to you and the object goes into production.
personal.orderNote: The order is completed in the cabinet.

pricingPage.metaDescription: How a number's price is worked out, what the devices cost, what the monthly subscription buys and what happens if it lapses.
pricingPage.title: Pricing
pricingPage.lead: Everything is on this page: how a number's price is worked out, what a device costs, what the monthly subscription buys and what happens if the payments stop. Nobody has to be phoned to find out.
pricingPage.ruleTitle: The shape of the number sets the price
pricingPage.ruleBody: Every number is three letters and three digits: ABC123. The base price is the same for everyone. After that it is shape: the rarer the letters, the larger the multiplier, and the same again for the digits. Nothing else is added — which is why you can work out any number's price yourself.
pricingPage.formula: Base price × letter multiplier × digit multiplier
pricingPage.lettersBody: The list holds {rare} words people know, {top} of them status words — VIP, CEO, UZB and the like. Anything not on the list is judged on shape alone.
pricingPage.digitsBody: There is no list on this side, only shape. 777 is three of the same digit, 123 runs in order, 121 is a palindrome, 007 has two leading zeros.
pricingPage.tiersBody: Once the two multipliers are multiplied together, a number lands in one of five tiers. The tier does not change the price — it follows from it.
pricingPage.tierRareNote: One weak pattern on one side — a palindrome or something like it.
pricingPage.tierEpicNote: A strong pattern on one side: a word people know, or digits in a row.
pricingPage.tierLegendaryNote: A strong pattern on both sides.
pricingPage.tierGenesisNote: Both sides at their strongest. Very few are left.
pricingPage.examplesBody: The prices below are calculated from that same formula when the page is rendered — none of them is typed in by hand.
pricingPage.blockedTitle: Combinations that are not for sale
pricingPage.blockedBody: Some letter combinations are not sold at any price: the abbreviations of state bodies, obscenities and sacred names. Such a number looks in the search exactly like a number that does not exist, and it cannot be taken.
pricingPage.devicesBody: The device is paid for separately. A number is expensive because it is scarce; a device is expensive because it was manufactured. Fold them into one price and the owner of a rare number would be paying more for the same piece of steel.
pricingPage.subTitle: What the monthly payment is for
pricingPage.subBody: The number is bought once and stays yours. The subscription is for the profile being open every day, the statistics being collected and the contacts being kept. They are paid for separately because they are separate things: a number is issued once, a server costs money every month.
pricingPage.planFreeNote: Works from the day you take the number. Nothing more to pay.
pricingPage.planPremiumNote: Turns the profile from a display into something you work with.
planPremiumItems: Full analytics — by day and by link
Contacts collected, and an Excel export
The Flex mark is removed from the page
pricingPage.planYearly: A year up front is {price} so'm — twelve months for the price of {months}.
pricingPage.teamBody: Numbers bought for staff are {price} so'm a month per seat, {min} seats minimum. One invoice, one payment. Somebody leaves and the number stays with the company.
pricingPage.venueBody: A venue pays by how many points it has. A point is a table, a room, a door or a chair. The menu, the call button, the QR and the NFC are in the price.
pricingPage.lapsedBody: Everybody asks this one silently, so the answer stands here.
lapsedItems: The profile still opens — a tap on the card brings up the same page.
Editing closes: the profile falls back to the ordinary plan.
The number stays yours and nothing is deleted.
The day the payment resumes, everything is where it was.

business.lead: A table, a room, a stylist's chair, a doctor's door. Each gets its own NFC marker and its own page. The guest installs nothing — they hold their phone against it.
business.howLead: A point is a table, a room, a door or a treatment room. Each has its own marker and its own page, all edited from one panel.
